title: introduce lightweight presubmit router, lint telemetry, and dep-rotation adapter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add lightweight presubmit routing to speed feedback; introduce telemetry hooks for lint fastpath; integrate a dependency rotation adapter to reduce monorepo churn.
description: Motivation: our presubmit lanes are large and noisy for small changes, CI feedback is slow for developer iteration, and transitive dependency churn continues to cause flakey premerge failures. This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit router that routes edits through a fast-path lint runner for path-local changes, instrumentation hooks to surface lint/runtime telemetry, and a dependency-rotation adapter that automates a conservative rotation of devdeps on a scheduled cadence. Summary of changes and checklist: - introduce scripts/ci/presubmit-router.ts to detect change surface and pick fast lanes for lint/quick-tests - add .github/workflows/presubmit-fastpath.yml that runs an opt-in fast lint path for small PRs - add telemetry hooks (telemetry/lint-hooks.ts) that emit per-lint-run duration, cache-hit, and rule-count tags to our internal metrics sink - wire lightweight runner into existing presubmit dispatcher with safe fallbacks to the full presubmit pipeline - implement tools/dep-rotation/adapter that can generate candidate bump PRs for developer review and emit a compatibility report - update developer-contrib.md with new presubmit guidelines and examples - small packaging updates (package.json scripts, Makefile targets) - add a smoke harness for release pipelines to validate the presubmit router under a production-like event (tools/release-smoke/) Checklist: [x] Unit tests for presubmit-router logic [x] E2E smoke runner added and exercised locally [x] Telemetry schema reviewed with data-platform (ENG-2203) [x] Docs updated in contributor guidelines [x] Gradual rollout plan added in PR notes Testing notes: local unit tests, a small matrix of Node/Go test runners and an isolated CI run were executed. The integration job failed once on an unrelated docker image pull flake and was re-run; final CI green. Rollout plan: enable presubmit-fastpath as opt-in via repo label and progressively enable for low-risk repos. Fallback: presubmit-router falls back to main presubmit pipeline when any heuristics are ambiguous or when telemetry indicates a sustained error rate. Why distinct from previous work: previous PRs optimized CI caching and shard split; this focuses on routing logic, observability for lint fastpaths, and an automated yet conservative dependency rotation mechanism to reduce manual churn.

review_comments: Owen Patel: Nice separation — can we guard the fastpath to only run for < 10-file diffs initially? Added a suggestion to the router heuristics.
Maya Chen (author): Good call — added a max-files threshold default to 8 and a repo opt-in label; preserved fallback behavior when threshold exceeded.
Ravi Singh: Telemetry looks useful; please add a metric for cache-hit-rate and ensure the emitted tags are stable (avoid high cardinality).
Maya Chen (author): Added cache_hit boolean and lint_rule_count integer tag; removed file-level tags to limit cardinality.

Elena Morales: dep-rotation PR generator is neat but make sure the adapter labels generated PRs with 'dep-rotation' and includes a human-readable compatibility summary. Also requested an explicit opt-out via .dep-rotate-ignore.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented label + compat-report and added .dep-rotate-ignore parsing.
notes: Deployment/rollout: presubmit-fastpath is feature-flagged; operations will observe new telemetry (metric names: ci.presubmit.lint.duration, ci.presubmit.lint.cache_hit, ci.presubmit.lint.rule_count). The dep-rotation adapter is scheduled in staging for a two-week experiment; generated PRs are labelled and require human approval. Backout: remove the opt-in label to disable fastpath immediately. Monitoring: alerts added for >5% error rate or increased presubmit failure rate after rollout.
ci_investigation_log: During CI run on 2026-02-20 an unrelated docker hub rate-limit caused a transient failure in the e2e-matrix job; we retried and added a retry wrapper around docker pulls in runner-wrapper.sh to reduce flakes.
